highlights:
# Authentication and permissions

To keep Squarespace merchant site data private and secure, every request to Commerce APIs must be authenticated and have minimum permissions. However, authenticated requests automatically have access to public site data, such as site name, identifier, language, currency, time zone, and location.

Read the permission levels for each Commerce API below. Then, depending on your development needs, authenticate requests by using an API key or OAuth access token.

> Remember: Requests only have access to data for the website that owns the API key or OAuth access token.

## API permission levels

Forms API

- Read Only: View form submission data; for Zapier integration only

Inventory API

- Read Only: View inventory stock levels
- Read and Write: Manage inventory stock levels

Orders API

- Read Only: View order, fulfillment, and customer information (name, email, address, and more)
- Read and Write: View customer information (name, email, address, and more); manage order and fulfillment information

Products API

- Read Only: View product information, including information for any images and variants; view Store Page information
- Read and Write: Manage product information, including information for any images and variants; view Store Page information

Contacts API

- Read Only: View contact records, address books, and marketing preferences
- Read and Write: Manage contact records, address books, and marketing preferences

Discounts API

- Read Only: View discount records
- Read and Write: Manage discount records

Webhook Subscriptions API (OAuth only)

- Read and Write: Create, update, delete, and test webhook subscriptions

Profiles API (maintenance mode — new integrations should use the Contacts API)

- Read Only: View the name, address, email, marketing preferences, and other profile information of customers, subscribers, and other website users

Transactions API

- Read Only: View transactional order, donation data, and customer information (email)

## Authenticating requests

Depending on your development needs, you can use a generated API key or start the OAuth process with Squarespace to become a registered OAuth client. A Squarespace merchant site can use both API keys and OAuth for data access, but Squarespace Extensions are required to use OAuth.

### Custom applications

With Squarespace's Commerce Advanced plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site.

Follow the steps below to generate an API key for a custom application.

1. Log in to a Squarespace site.
2. In the left nav, click Settings; scroll down and click Advanced.
3. Click Developer API Keys.
4. Click the GENERATE KEY button.
5. In the dialog, add a key name under "KEY NAME", and select one or more Commerce APIs under "PERMISSIONS" and permission level.
6. Record the generated key in a safe and secure place.

For security reasons, this is the only time the API key is visible. API keys will never expire as long as the merchant site remains active.

### Commercial development

Squarespace Extensions allow customers on any plan to optimize and expand their site in a few clicks. If you'd like to develop a new Extension, start the OAuth client process here. Once you've obtained OAuth credentials, you can use our OAuth 2.0 Guide to learn how to authorize your application to integrate with Squarespace and use Squarespace APIs. Registering an OAuth client, and having it reviewed and approved, only allows OAuth connections with Squarespace. It doesn't list your application in Squarespace Extensions, which is a separate process.

highlights:
# Accessing Squarespace APIs using OAuth 2.0

Squarespace uses OAuth 2.0 to authorize third-party applications to integrate with Squarespace and consume Squarespace APIs.

## Terms

| Client | Third-party application that needs to make Squarespace API calls. |
| --- | --- |
| User | Squarespace customer who wants to integrate their site with a client. |
| Confirmation page | Page created by Squarespace for the user to authorize (Allow or Deny) client access to their Squarespace account. |
| Access token | Short-term token to make authenticated API requests. |
| Refresh token | Long-term token to obtain new access tokens. |

## Instructions

### 1. Register the client and obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials

Before a client can make Squarespace API calls, the client must be registered with Squarespace as an OAuth client. Start the Oauth client process here.

- Client name
- Icon image (.png or .svg format, max size 200kb, 1:1 ratio)
- Redirect URI(s) - For example, `https://thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/connect`
- Initiate URL* - For example, `https://thirdpartyapp.com/oauth/initiate`.
- Link to Client's Terms and Conditions
- Link to Client's Privacy Policy

*Applies only to Squarespace partner apps. These will be linked from inside Squarespace.

We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible. These credentials are used in the subsequent steps.

### 2. Prompt the user to authorize client access

The `/authorize` URL prompts the user to authorize client access to their Squarespace data and serves as the confirmation page. If a user selects Allow, OAuth 2.0 authentication is started between the client and Squarespace APIs. Append required and any optional parameters to the `GET /authorize` endpoint; all parameter values should be URL-encoded.

`GET https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize`

| Query parameter | Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client_id` | Required | Alphanumeric value for your_client_id that was supplied by Squarespace in Step 1. |
| `redirect_uri` | Required | String; the full redirect URI sent to Squarespace in Step 1. |
| `scope` | Required | String; comma-separated list of client permission values (see below) for API access. The confirmation page always displays website(s) for user selection for `scope=website.*`  `website.orders` Send order data and mark orders as fulfilled. `website.orders.read` View order and fulfillment information. `website.transactions.read` Access transactional order and donation data. `website.inventory` View and update inventory stock levels. `website.inventory.read` View inventory stock levels. `website.products` View product information and modify products. `website.products.read` View product information. `website.contacts` View customer contact information and address book entries; create, update, and delete contacts and address book entries. `website.contacts.read` View customer contact information and address book entries. `website.discounts` View and manage discounts. `website.discounts.read` View discounts. Example: `&scope=website.inventory,website.orders` |
| `state` | Required | Alphanumeric random value generated by client. You'll use it in Step 3, Implement redirect URI, to prevent CSRF attacks. |
| `website_id` | Conditionally Required | Alphanumeric value for a Squarespace site ID. When a logged-in user initiates an OAuth connection from Squarespace, this value is appended as a query parameter on the provided initiate URL. Partners must pass this parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint. If an OAuth connection is initiated by a logged-out user, Squarespace will not include a website_id parameter on the initiate URL. Partners should not pass any `website_id` parameter back to the `GET /authorize` endpoint in these cases. Instead, the user will be prompted to select a website on the confirmation page. |
| `access_type` | Optional | String; use `offline` for long-term API access. For more information, see Token expiration and long-term access. Omit parameter for short-term API access. |

Authorize URL example with parameters

Note: Parameter values are in plain text and not URL-encoded for example purposes.

`https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/authorize?client_id=fGBjMDBaUHli&redirect_uri=http://localhost:8090/oauth/callback&scope=website.inventory,website.orders&state=2BsmGS9AAzFppUmcoIagOLj4iKII`

### 3. Implement redirect URI

Both Allow or Deny on the confirmation page directs the user to the client redirect URI (i.e., the `redirect_uri` specified in Step 2) with query parameters appended by Squarespace. For Allow, the redirect URI should verify the `state` parameter and match it against `state` value that was appended for the `/authorize` endpoint. This verification prevents CSRF attacks. Squarespace doesn't provide guidelines for Deny implementation.

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `error` | String; `access_denied` if user selects Deny on confirmation page. Parameter isn't appended if user selects Allow. |
| `state` | Alphanumeric value; not present if user selects Deny. |
| `code` | Alphanumeric value used in step 4. Request access token. Value is initially URL-encoded and should be decoded prior to sending in the access token request. Valid for two minutes and only for one-time use. Not present if user selects Deny. |

### 4. Request access token

`POST https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/oauth/provider/tokens`

The client makes a `POST /tokens` call with required and any optional parameters for an access token from Squarespace. Access tokens in the response are only valid for 30 minutes. For more information, see Token expiration and long-term access.

| Body | Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grant_type` | Optional | String; default is `authorization_code`; use `authorization_code` for your first request. For long-term API access, use `refresh_token` for all subsequent requests. |
| `code` | Required if `grant_type=authorization_code` | Alphanumeric value of code passed to redirect URI. |
| `redirect_uri` | Required if `grant_type=authorization_code` | String; redirect_uri used for the `/authorize` endpoint. |
| `refresh_token` | Required if `grant_type=refresh_token` | String; use application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded |
| Header |  |  |
| `Authorization` | Required | Follow the steps below to build the header value:  Use your Squarespace OAuth 2.0 credentials to construct a string in the format: `your_client_id:your_client_secret`  Encode the string from Step 1 into base-64   Add Basic<space> as a prefix to the encoded string from Step 2   Example your_client_id: abc123 your_client_secret: 12secret345  Authorization after base-64 Basic YWJjMTIzOjEyc2VjcmV0MzQ1 |
| `Content-Type` | Required | String; use application/json or application/x-www-form-urlencoded |
| `User-Agent` | Required | String; If you see an error referencing SEC-43, a User-Agent header is missing |

`{
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "access_token": "T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB...",
  // expires 30 minutes after it's created ...
  "access_token_expires_at": "1553532363.542",
}`

### 5. Make API requests

After you obtain an access token, you can make API requests.

Endpoint:

`https://api.squarespace.com/...`

Authorization format:

`Bearer<space><access-token-from-tokens-response>`

Using the sample response from Step 4, `Authorization` would have the value:

`Bearer T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB...`

## Token expiration and long-term access

When a response from `POST /tokens` is received, `access_token` is only valid for 30 minutes. For long-term Squarespace API access, the client has to prompt the user to reauthorize using the `GET /authorize` endpoint or use refresh tokens.

### Refresh tokens

To get a refresh token, add `access_type=offline` as a parameter to the `GET /authorize` request. When the client makes a `POST /tokens` call, the response includes `refresh_token`. Use the refresh token to get new tokens by making another `POST /tokens` call with the parameters below. The refresh token expires after seven days.

- `grant_type=refresh_token`
- `refresh_token=<previous-refresh-token-value>`

Note: Each `POST /tokens` call with a `refresh_token` parameter results in a new `refresh_token` and `access_token`. Refresh tokens are effectively one-time use—the original refresh token is invalidated as soon as the new access token is used. If long-term API access is required, the client should replace the stored refresh token with the most recent `refresh_token`. Note that obtaining new tokens doesn't revoke existing access tokens.

Sample response from `/tokens`:

`{
  "token": "T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB...",
  "token_type": "bearer",

  // expires 30 mins after creation
  "access_token": "T1|Rr0Wc95uu3cSeBh06yB...",
  "access_token_expires_at": "1553532363.542",

  // expires 7 days after creation
  "refresh_token": "1|KYUYh35zcwzx4Zt/oty3...",
  "refresh_token_expires_at": "1554135363.542"
}`

Sample use case

...

4. Client repeats Steps 2 and 3 indefinitely.

### Invalid tokens and revoking access

Tokens become invalid in two ways: the tokens expire or the user revokes client access from the Squarespace UI. In either case, the user has to reauthorize client access to get new access tokens.

When an access token is invalid, Squarespace responds to API requests with `401 Unauthorized`. If a client receives a 401, they should notify the user that their Squarespace integration requires reauthorization.

auth.title: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs
highlights:
## 1. Generate an API key or start the OAuth process

If you don't have an API key or are a registered OAuth client already, read the Authentication and permissions guide.

## 2. Format your request headers

For a successful request, every Commerce API request must use the headers and URL format shown below. The current version number for each API is located on the API's overview page. To learn more about versioning, read the Versioning guide.

> Caution: All requests sent over HTTP instead of HTTPS are rejected.

`curl "https://api.squarespace.com/{api-version}/{resource-path}" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN" \
  -H "User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION" \

  // Add a Content-Type header when making requests with a body.
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"`

### Recommendations

Accept header: it's okay to use one, but not necessary  Although an `Accept` header is conventional in HTTPS requests, it's not necessary as Commerce APIs support JSON responses only.

User-Agent header: it's okay to use default values for testing, but not recommended  Default values for `User-Agent` are often injected by HTTP client applications (e.g.`"User-Agent: curl/7.54.0"`). Although they're okay to use, doing so may be subject to stricter rate limiting. Requests without a `User-Agent` header are rejected.

## API key security

Your unique API key is a randomized string of characters which permits authenticated access to your Squarespace account.

To create a new key:

1. Open the Developer tools panel.
2. Click Developer API Keys.
3. Click Generate Key. 
4. Enter a Key Name.
5. Under Permissions, check Orders, Forms, Inventory, or Transactions. Forms are available in the Business plan or higher. Orders, Inventory, and Transactions are only available in the Commerce Advanced plan.
6. Select the permissions for the API key.
7. Click Next.
8. Copy your unique API key.

When you get this key:

- Keep it secure. Treat your API key like you would treat any account password.
- Copy and save it for your records. For security, we don’t store your API key. There’s no way to retrieve it after you close the window, but if you lose it, you can always create a new one.

You can follow these steps again to create multiple keys.

highlights:
# Announcing Self-Service OAuth Credential Management

Date: Monday, July 27, 2026

Starting Monday, July 27, 2026, Squarespace is transitioning to a self-service model for OAuth credential management, empowering developers to build and maintain integrations with greater speed and autonomy.

## What is changing?

Historically, obtaining OAuth credentials to work with Squarespace APIs required manual form submissions and Zendesk tickets, often resulting in wait times of several days. With this launch, we are introducing a new "Developer Apps" tab within the Account Dashboard, allowing you to bypass manual provisioning.

### Key Features

- Instant Credential Generation: Generate OAuth client IDs and secrets immediately for development and testing.
- On-Demand Secret Rotation: Securely rotate client secrets through the self-service interface to maintain high security standards without reaching out to support.
- Unified Management: Create, update, and view application details in a single dashboard.

## Demo Mode and Production Reviews

To ensure platform security while maintaining developer speed, all new applications created via the self-service tool will enter Demo Mode by default.

When you are ready to take your integration live, simply request a review directly from the app details page in your dashboard.

Approval takes your app out of Demo Mode. It doesn't list your app in Squarespace Extensions, which is a separate process.

## How to Get Started

1. Visit the Portal: Navigate to developers.squarespace.com and select Start Building on our homepage.
2. Accept Terms: You will be prompted to accept the mandatory Developer Terms of Use to unlock the new functionality.
3. Manage Credentials: Access the Developers tab in your Account Dashboard to begin creating your first app.

Note for Existing Users: This change applies to new OAuth applications. Existing OAuth users who wish to utilize the self-service management screen should create a new app through the dashboard and request a review.

gate.title: Partners — Squarespace
highlights:
### What does it mean to partner with Squarespace?

A partnership is a collaboration that helps people discover, use, or get more value from Squarespace products. Depending on your organization and goals, that could mean building an app or integration, reselling eligible products, referring new customers, or working with Squarespace through a professional partner program.

### What is a reseller partner?

A reseller partner offers eligible Squarespace products to its own customers, often as part of its existing service or customer experience. Depending on the arrangement, a partner may integrate with Squarespace’s Reseller API or use another approved referral or sales path. Reseller partners don’t need to become accredited domain registrars themselves, but they must be approved and operate under the applicable program terms. Learn about domain reselling.

### What is an app or extension partner?

An app or extension partner builds a third-party tool that connects with Squarespace to help customers run or grow their websites and businesses. Some integrations may be eligible for inclusion in one of our directories, such as Squarespace Extensions or Acuity Integrations. A directory listing is subject to applicable review and approval; submitting an inquiry does not guarantee acceptance or listing.

### What is an integrated partner?

“Integrated partner” describes a partner whose product or service connects with Squarespace—for example, through an API or an extension. It describes the nature of the technical connection, not one universal partner program. An integration may or may not also be listed in one of our directories, involve a reseller relationship, or include a commercial agreement.

### What is an affiliate partner?

An affiliate partner promotes Squarespace using tracked links. If a referred, first-time customer makes a qualifying purchase, an approved affiliate may earn a commission under the Affiliate Program’s terms. Applications are reviewed, and payout details are provided through the program. Explore the Squarespace Affiliate Program.

### Is Squarespace Circle the same as the Affiliate Program?

No. Squarespace Circle is a partner program for freelancers and agencies who build websites for clients on Squarespace. Circle offers program benefits for eligible members; referral payments require separate registration. The Affiliate Program is a separate application-based program for partners who refer new customers through tracked links. Compare the programs and explore Circle.

...

### Which partnership path is right for my organization?

- Choose an integration path if you have a product that could connect to Squarespace and benefit customers.
- Explore reselling if you want to offer eligible Squarespace products within your own customer experience.
- Explore affiliate if you have an audience and want to refer prospective customers using tracked links.
- Explore Squarespace Circle if you build Squarespace websites for clients.
- If your idea doesn’t fit neatly into one of these paths, tell us about it through the partner inquiry form.

### What are the benefits of partnering with Squarespace?

Benefits depend on the partnership type and any applicable approval or agreement. Depending on the path, a partnership may offer product distribution or discovery, a way to serve shared customers, referral or reseller earnings, technical resources, or marketing opportunities. No benefit, listing, payment, or level of support is guaranteed unless it is included in the relevant program terms or agreement.

### Are there fees, commissions, or revenue-sharing terms?

There is no single commercial model for every partnership. Affiliate commissions, reseller economics, app pricing, and any other commercial terms are determined by the applicable program terms or a separate agreement. Review the terms for your specific program before participating. Squarespace Circle is free to join; other partnership paths may have different requirements or terms.

### Do I need to be an existing Squarespace customer?

It depends on the program. Squarespace Circle is for Squarespace customers who build websites for clients. Other partner paths have their own requirements; check the relevant program information or share your proposal with the partner team.

### Does submitting an inquiry guarantee approval, an integration, or an Extensions listing?

No. Each opportunity is evaluated for fit, customer value, technical and operational readiness, and applicable program requirements. Approval to explore a partnership does not by itself guarantee a contract, API access, launch, directory listing, or marketing support.

### What technical or review steps should I expect?

For integrations, the steps depend on the APIs, permissions, and product experience involved. Partners should review the applicable developer documentation and terms before building. Additional technical, security, privacy, product, or listing reviews may apply.

### How long does it take to become a partner?

There isn’t one timeline for every partner type. Timing depends on the program, the information provided, technical scope, and any required reviews or agreements. The partner team can discuss likely next steps after learning more about your proposal.

...

### How do I get started or share a partnership idea?

Choose the program page above if you already know which path fits. Otherwise, tell us about your organization, product or audience, the customers you serve, and what you’d like to accomplish with Squarespace using the Partner inquiry form. We’ll route your inquiry to the appropriate team.

Before a client can make Squarespace API calls, the client must be registered with Squarespace as an OAuth client. Start the Oauth client process here.

*Applies only to Squarespace partner apps. These will be linked from inside Squarespace.

We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible. These credentials are used in the subsequent steps.

### 2. Prompt the user to authorize client access

The `/authorize` URL prompts the user to authorize client access to their Squarespace data and serves as the confirmation page. If a user selects Allow, OAuth 2.0 authentication is started between the client and Squarespace APIs. Append required and any optional parameters to the `GET /authorize` endpoint; all parameter values should be URL-encoded.

...

## Token expiration and long-term access

When a response from `POST /tokens` is received, `access_token` is only valid for 30 minutes. For long-term Squarespace API access, the client has to prompt the user to reauthorize using the `GET /authorize` endpoint or use refresh tokens.

mcp.title: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs
highlights:
# Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server

The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation.

With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer.

Connect a Client → Add Squarespace to Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP client.

Notice: If you are a Squarespace user who is accessing the Squarespace MCP server through an AI assistant, for example to search for a domain or manage your own website, your use is governed by our Terms of Service. If you're a developer building an experience for your users and connecting your own app or agent directly to the Squarespace MCP server, for example to add domain search to your product, your use is governed by our Developer Terms of Use.

## What you can do

The server's tools are organized into groups. Each group has its own page describing what its tools do, what to ask for, and what to watch out for.

| Group | What it's for | Sign-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Domains | Brainstorm business names, check domain availability and pricing, and get a link to buy a domain on Squarespace. | Not required |
| Commerce | Find, create, and update contacts and products, and look up orders, on one of your websites. Currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. | Required |

## How it works

The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server. There's nothing to install. Your MCP client connects directly to:

`https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp`

You don't call the tools yourself. You ask the assistant for something in plain language, and it decides which tools to call and in what order. The tool descriptions the assistant needs are sent by the server when it connects, so they don't need to be copied into your prompts.

### Signing in

The Domains tools work for anyone, with no Squarespace account required.

The Commerce tools read and change a website, so they need you to sign in with your Squarespace account. They only appear in your client once you've signed in, and they act with your own permissions: an assistant can only see and change what you could see and change yourself in that website's Commerce panel. See Connect a Client.

### Working with a website

Every signed-in tool works on one website at a time. If it isn't clear which site you mean, the assistant will ask, then keep using that site for the rest of the conversation until you ask to switch.

### What the tools can and can't change

- Domains tools never buy anything. They return a checkout link. A domain is only registered when someone opens that link and completes checkout on squarespace.com.
- Commerce tools don't move money. They can create and update contacts and products, but they can't take payments, issue refunds, or fulfill orders. Orders are read-only.
- Changes are real. A product or contact the assistant creates or edits is saved to your live website. New products are hidden from shoppers until you (or the assistant, if you ask) publish them.

Most MCP clients ask you to approve a tool before it makes a change. Keep that approval step turned on for tools that write to your website.

## Supported clients

Squarespace is built into Gemini as a connected app, and the Domains tools also work in Claude, ChatGPT, and any client that supports remote MCP servers. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. See Connect a Client for setup steps.

mcp.title: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs
highlights:
# Domains

The Domains tools help someone go from an idea to a domain they can buy on Squarespace, without leaving the chat. They work for anyone, in Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, and other assistants, with no Squarespace account or sign-in needed.

These tools never register a domain or take payment. Each available domain comes with a checkout link, and the domain is only bought when someone opens that link and completes checkout on squarespace.com, where it can also be paired with a website and professional email.

## Tools

| What it does | Tool name |
| --- | --- |
| Brainstorm business names | `domains_generate_names` |
| Search for a domain | `domains_search` |

A typical conversation uses both: if someone describes their business but doesn't have a name yet, the assistant suggests names first, then checks domains for the most promising ones.

Your client may show the tool name when it asks you to approve a tool, so each section below lists it too.

### Brainstorm business names

Tool name: `domains_generate_names`

Suggests names for a business, product, or project, grouped by tone: neutral, playful, professional, friendly, informative, and quirky. These are name ideas, not domains, so the assistant then checks which ones are available as domains.

Try asking:

> "Help me come up with a name for a ceramics studio in Portland that focuses on classes."

> "I need a domain for my bakery."

What to tell the assistant

- What your business or idea is about, in a sentence or two. The more specific, the better: where it is, who it's for, and what makes it different.

### Search for a domain

Tool name: `domains_search`

Checks whether a domain is available and what it costs, and suggests alternatives. For each available domain you get the first-year price, the renewal price, and a link to buy it on Squarespace. If the exact domain you asked for is taken, the assistant tells you and shows available alternatives.

Try asking:

> "Is sarahbakes.com available, and what are some alternatives under $20 a year?"

> "Find me domains for Nova Labs."

What to tell the assistant

- A name, keyword, or exact domain you have in mind, such as "Nova Labs" or "sarahbakes.com".

Ways to narrow it down

- More or fewer suggestions
- Include domains that are already taken, to see what exists
- Quick ideas only, without checking availability or prices

Good to know

- The purchase link opens Squarespace checkout with the domain already in the cart. It tells Squarespace which assistant the purchase came from, but nothing about your conversation.
- This tool doesn't look up who owns a domain, change DNS or hosting settings, or manage a domain you already own.

## Prompts

Prompts are ready-made starting points that some clients show as commands or suggestions, for example as a `/` command. Choosing one starts a conversation that uses the tools above.

| Prompt | When to use it | What it asks you for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `find_domain` | You've described what you want to build but haven't picked a name yet. | What your site or business is about. |
| `check_domain` | You have a specific domain in mind and want to know if it's available and what it costs. | The domain to check. |
| `purchase_domain` | You want to buy or register a domain. | What the domain is for, or a name you have in mind. If you don't say, the assistant asks. |

mcp.title: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs
highlights:
# Commerce

The Commerce tools let an AI assistant work with the store on one of your Squarespace websites: find and update customer contacts, look up orders, and create and edit products. Ask in plain language, such as "which orders still need fulfilling?" or "add a new t-shirt product for $15", and the assistant picks the right tools.

## Before you start

- Sign in. These tools appear after you sign in to Squarespace in your client. They act as you, with your permissions on the website.
- Pick a website. Every Commerce tool works on one website. If it isn't clear which site you mean, the assistant will ask.
- Use Claude or ChatGPT. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. Other clients, including Gemini, only get the Domains tools.

## What these tools can and can't do

- They can search, read, create, and update contacts and products, and search and read orders.
- They can't take payments, issue refunds, fulfill or cancel orders, or delete anything.
- Changes are saved to your live store. New products are hidden from shoppers until they're published, so you can review them first.

AI assistants can make mistakes. They might misread a request, pick the wrong contact or product, or describe a change that didn't happen the way they say. Before you approve a change, check what the assistant is about to do, and keep your client's approval prompts turned on. Afterwards, check important changes in your Squarespace dashboard.

What these tools return, including your customers' names, email addresses, postal addresses, and order history, is shared with the company behind your assistant, such as Anthropic or OpenAI. Check your assistant's settings for how long it keeps your conversations and whether they're used to train its models.

## Tools

| Area | What it does | Tool name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contacts | Find contacts | `squarespace_query_contacts` |
| Contacts | Look up a contact | `squarespace_get_contact` |
| Contacts | Add a contact | `squarespace_create_contact` |
| Contacts | Update a contact | `squarespace_update_contact` |
| Orders | Find orders | `squarespace_query_orders` |
| Orders | Look up an order | `squarespace_get_order` |
| Products | Find products | `squarespace_query_products` |
| Products | Look up a product | `squarespace_get_product` |
| Products | List store pages | `squarespace_list_store_pages` |
| Products | Create a physical product | `squarespace_create_physical_product` |
| Products | Create a service product | `squarespace_create_service_product` |
| Products | Create a gift card | `squarespace_create_gift_card_product` |
| Products | Update a product | `squarespace_update_product` |

Your client may show the tool name when it asks you to approve a tool, so each section below lists it too.

...

Contacts are the customers and subscribers in your website's contact list.

...

## Orders

The Orders tools only read orders. They can't fulfill, cancel, or refund an order.

### Find orders

Tool name: `squarespace_query_orders`

Finds orders and gives you a short list with each order's number, dates, total, fulfillment and payment status, and the buyer's email. To see what's in an order, the assistant looks it up next.

Try asking:

> "Which orders still need fulfilling?"

> "What has alice@example.com ordered?"

> "What was refunded last month?"

Ways to narrow it down

- Fulfillment status: pending, fulfilled, or canceled
- Payment status, such as paid, refunded, pending, failed, or partially paid
- Who placed the order
- When the order was last changed

Good to know

- Dates mean "last changed", not "placed". An old order that was fulfilled yesterday counts as changed yesterday. You can't search by the date an order was placed.
- Some orders are left out unless you ask. If you don't mention a payment status, orders that are unpaid, failed, partially paid, or waiting on a refund aren't included. Ask for "all orders" to see them.

### Look up an order

Tool name: `squarespace_get_order`

Shows one order in full: who placed it, every item, the subtotal, tax, shipping, discounts, refunds and total, fulfillment and payment status, shipping and billing addresses, and the payments and refunds behind it.

...

## Products

The Products tools cover physical, service, gift card, and digital products. Digital products can be looked up and updated, but not created.

### Find products

Tool name: `squarespace_query_products`

Finds products and gives you a short list with each product's name, type, whether it's published, and its URL. To see prices, options, or stock, the assistant looks the product up next.

Try asking:

> "List my gift card products."

> "Find the blue hoodie."

Ways to narrow it down

- Product name
- Product type: physical, digital, service, or gift card
- When the product was last changed

### Look up a product

Tool name: `squarespace_get_product`

Shows one product in full: name, description, URL, whether it's published, tags, SEO title and description, images, and the store page it's on. For physical and service products it also shows each option (such as a size or color) with its SKU, price, sale price, and stock. Digital products have a single price instead.

...

### Create a physical product

Tool name: `squarespace_create_physical_product`

Creates a product that ships, such as clothing, prints, or home goods, with one or more options like sizes or colors.

> "Create a t-shirt in S, M and L for $25, with 10 of each in stock."

- What you're selling and its price
- Any options it comes in, such as sizes or colors, and the price of each if they differ
- A SKU for each option. If you don't use SKUs, ask the assistant to make them up.
- Which store page it goes on. The assistant can list your pages.

- How many you have in stock, or unlimited. If you don't say, it starts sold out.
- A sale price
- A description and tags
- The product's URL
- Weight and dimensions for shipping, barcode (GTIN), and manufacturer part number (MPN)
- Whether to publish it straight away. If you don't say, it's hidden.

### Create a service product

Tool name: `squarespace_create_service_product`

Creates a service, such as a class, a consultation, or a membership

...

### Update a product

Tool name: `squarespace_update_product`

Changes an existing product of any type in one go. Only what you mention is changed, and the assistant can tell you exactly what was updated. If one part of the change fails, the rest still goes through and the assistant can tell you which part didn't.

> "Put the blue hoodie on sale for $40."

> "Set the mug to unlimited stock and publish it."

...

- Name, description, URL, and tags
- SEO title and description
- Whether it's published or hidden
- Prices and sale prices
- Stock, as a number or unlimited
- Add or remove options, such as a new size. A product always keeps at least one.
- SKU, weight and dimensions, barcode (GTIN), and MPN

- It can't add a new kind of option, such as adding colors to a product that only comes in sizes. Do that in the Commerce panel on Squarespace first.

mcp.title: Squarespace MCP Server — MCP Server | APIs.io
highlights:
# Squarespace MCP Server

Squarespace operates a first-party REMOTE MCP server at https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp. It answers an unauthenticated JSON-RPC tools/list with HTTP 200 and returns two real tools with full JSON Schema inputSchemas. The tool list was captured verbatim to mcp/squarespace-mcp-tools.json on 2026-08-13. Note what it is and is not: this server exposes the DOMAIN acquisition funnel — domain search and brand-name generation — not the Commerce APIs. None of the 55 published Commerce operations (orders, products, inventory, contacts, discounts, transactions, webhooks) are reachable through it. It is a customer-acquisition surface an agent can call on an end user's behalf, not an agent interface to a merchant's store.

...

## Tools

- `domains_search` — Search Squarespace's domain catalog for a keyword. Returns availability, pricing, and a pre-rendered purchase link per domain.
- `domains_generate_names` — Generate brand/business NAME IDEAS from a free-text description, when the user describes a business or idea but doesn't have a name yet.

...

## About MCP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol Anthropic introduced for connecting LLM-based agents to external tools and data sources. Providers publish MCP servers that expose their API surface as structured, discoverable tools — an MCP-compatible client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, etc.) can connect to the server and call its tools without any per-provider integration code.
